findings.evidence_excerpt: “universities across the sector” and “administrators everywhere face the same fundamental tension”
findings.recommendation: Recast these as bounded interpretations of the three-case sample, specify the national-system context, and reserve sector-wide claims for future comparative research.
findings.summary: The central contribution is overgeneralized from three institutions and 12 administrator interviews to the higher-education sector as a whole.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “A minority of participants expressed more skeptical or dissenting views ... these were excluded for space”
findings.recommendation: Analyze and report the dissenting accounts as negative cases, explain their relationship to the three themes, and revise claims of balanced or comprehensive representation accordingly.
findings.summary: The manuscript reports selectively excluding dissenting accounts, undermining the credibility of its claimed thematic account.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “our findings align with Delacroix (2018), who recommends ... broad stakeholder consultation as the central mechanism”
findings.recommendation: Replace this attribution with the manuscript's earlier account of Delacroix as cautioning against consultation-as-ritual, or substantiate a different source.
findings.summary: The policy recommendation misstates the cited literature, creating a claim-to-source contradiction.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “the first comprehensive account of how university administrators experience and enact QA implementation”
findings.recommendation: Qualify this as a contribution within the sampled national context and study design, or provide a systematic literature basis.
findings.summary: The paper's novelty claim is not calibrated to the evidence provided or to the literature review.

findings.evidence_excerpt: Abstract: “Fourteen administrators were interviewed”; Methods: “Twelve senior administrators (n=12)”
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the participant count throughout and state any exclusions and the final analytic sample.
findings.summary: The reported administrator sample size is internally inconsistent.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “achieved balanced representation of perspectives, capturing the full range”
findings.recommendation: Remove or materially qualify this assertion; describe the reported themes as dominant themes among the analyzed accounts.
findings.summary: The manuscript claims balanced, full-range representation while admitting that dissenting views were omitted.

agent_reports.role: journal fit, contribution, and claim calibration

findings.evidence_excerpt: “Fourteen administrators were interviewed in depth” / “Twelve senior administrators (n=12) ... were recruited”
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the discrepancy everywhere and state the final analytic sample, any exclusions, and whether all interviews contributed to the reported themes.
findings.summary: The reported interview sample size is internally inconsistent, making the qualitative evidentiary base indeterminate.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “capturing the full range of administrator views” ... “these were excluded for space, as they fell outside the three-theme structure”
findings.recommendation: Analyze and report dissenting or negative cases and revise claims of balanced or full representation.
findings.summary: The analysis explicitly excluded dissenting accounts to preserve a three-theme structure, risking selective thematic reporting.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “Twelve senior administrators ... were recruited through institutional QA offices.”
findings.recommendation: Specify sampling logic, eligibility, recruitment, participation counts, role and institution distribution, and gatekeeper effects.
findings.summary: The sampling strategy is insufficiently specified and recruitment through QA offices may have selected institutionally connected or favorable participants.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “Coding proceeded iteratively, moving between transcripts and an emerging set of themes until a stable structure was reached.”
findings.recommendation: Describe researcher roles, analytic orientation, coding stages, codebook revision, theme review, discrepant interpretations, and audit materials.
findings.summary: The thematic-analysis account lacks coder, code-development, disagreement, and traceability detail.

findings.evidence_excerpt: The methods describe recruitment, interviews, and iterative coding but do not identify interviewer or researcher positionality.
findings.recommendation: Add a reflexivity statement addressing relationships to QA and institutions, assumptions, and practices used to examine their influence.
findings.summary: No reflexivity account is provided despite possible professional proximity, power relations, and socially desirable responses.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “These themes emerged systematically ... giving us confidence” / “recurred across every interview.”
findings.recommendation: Report theme distribution, audit procedures, peer debriefing or participant feedback where used, and exception analysis; otherwise temper the claims.
findings.summary: Trustworthiness is asserted rather than demonstrated.

agent_reports.role: qualitative design, sampling, coding, reflexivity, and trustworthiness

findings.evidence_excerpt: §2 says Delacroix “argues against” consultation as sufficient evidence; §5 says he “recommends ... broad stakeholder consultation as the central mechanism.”
findings.recommendation: Correct the attribution and treat participation as necessary but not sufficient, paired with trust, substantive shared decision-making, and observable improvement.
findings.summary: The discussion reverses Delacroix (2018)'s stated position, making a core governance recommendation rest on a contradictory interpretation.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “universities across the sector”; “a general account of how the higher education sector as a whole constructs quality culture”; “administrators everywhere”
findings.recommendation: Limit conclusions to the sampled national system and make cross-sector or cross-national applicability a question for future testing.
findings.summary: The manuscript generalizes from three universities in one national system to the whole sector and to administrators everywhere.

findings.evidence_excerpt: The review cites Pettersen (2022) and Rahman (2020), while the conclusion claims “the first comprehensive account.”
findings.recommendation: Remove or substantiate the novelty claim and specify the study's incremental contribution relative to those works.
findings.summary: The first-comprehensive-account claim is not distinguished from cited work on distributed leadership and QA professional identity.

agent_reports.role: higher-education governance accuracy and literature positioning

findings.evidence_excerpt: “Twelve senior administrators ... were recruited”; “an ongoing negotiation among administrators, academics, and external bodies.”
findings.recommendation: Limit conclusions to administrators' perceived negotiation, or collect and analyze other groups' perspectives.
findings.summary: The paper treats administrator accounts as evidence of negotiation among administrators, academics, and external bodies although it collected no data from the latter groups.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “capturing the full range”; “these were excluded for space.”
findings.recommendation: Analyze and report dissenting accounts and remove balance or full-representation claims unless supported by the revised analysis.
findings.summary: Excluding dissenting administrator accounts while claiming balanced and full representation can materially distort participant meaning.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “the quality director of the largest private university in the region”; “all data were fully anonymized.”
findings.recommendation: Broaden or remove identifying role-institution combinations and reassess consent and residual disclosure risk.
findings.summary: Distinctive institutional and role details create a deductive-disclosure risk despite the assertion of full anonymization.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “consultation is not enough”; “consultation as the central mechanism.”
findings.recommendation: Correct the attribution and qualify consultation as conditional on evidence of influence, trust, and ownership.
findings.summary: The consultation recommendation conflicts with the manuscript's own account of Delacroix and is not validated by data from consulted groups.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “three universities in a single national system” ... “universities across the sector” ... “administrators everywhere”
findings.recommendation: Restrict conclusions to the sample and national context, state transferability conditions, and frame broader claims as hypotheses.
findings.summary: Sector-wide transferability claims exceed what a purposive, single-system three-university sample can support.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “capturing the full range” ... “these were excluded for space.”
findings.recommendation: Report the dissenting accounts and revise claims of balance, completeness, and prevalence.
findings.summary: Excluding dissenting accounts while claiming full-range representation creates selective-evidence risk.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “until a stable structure was reached” and “giving us confidence that the pattern was not an artifact.”
findings.recommendation: Specify code-development chronology, stopping rationale, negative-case handling, and institutional contribution to themes, or soften the claims.
findings.summary: The manuscript asserts saturation or stability without documenting how it was assessed.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “48 mid-level staff” ... “The survey corroborated the qualitative picture” ... “moderately positive ... score.”
findings.recommendation: Describe the survey as contextual or contrasting unless constructs map directly to interview themes; report the instrument, response rate, and integration logic.
findings.summary: The survey is said to corroborate the qualitative findings despite a different respondent group and a directionally mixed result.

findings.evidence_excerpt: “n=9” ... “n=11” ... “p<.05” ... “possible moderator.”
findings.recommendation: Report test, group statistics, effect size, exact p-value, assumptions, and multiplicity handling; treat it as exploratory and avoid institutional-type attribution.
findings.summary: The statistically significant institutional comparison is underreported and based on very small subgroups.

agent_reports.role: stress-test saturation, transferability, and evidentiary claims

accepted_findings.summary: The qualitative interview sample is internally inconsistent: the abstract reports 14 administrators, while Methods reports 12, leaving the analytic evidence base unclear.
The study claims balanced, full-range representation while deliberately excluding dissenting accounts, creating selective thematic reporting risk.
Sector-wide and universal claims substantially exceed a three-university, single-national-system sample.
The conclusion treats administrator accounts as evidence of a negotiation involving academics and external bodies, without data from those groups.
The discussion misattributes Delacroix's warning about consultation-as-ritual as an endorsement of consultation as the central mechanism.
The paper's first-comprehensive-account novelty claim is not calibrated to the literature it cites.
Sampling and QA-office recruitment are insufficiently specified, including potential gatekeeper effects.
The thematic-analysis description lacks enough detail to assess coding and theme-development rigor.
No reflexivity account addresses researcher proximity, power relations, or socially desirable responses.
Claims of systematic themes and cross-institutional coverage lack reported trustworthiness evidence.
Distinctive role and institutional details may permit deductive disclosure despite the anonymity claim.
Saturation or thematic stability is asserted without a documented assessment procedure.
The survey's claimed corroboration is unsupported because it concerns a different respondent group and a mixed result.
The small-subgroup statistical comparison is underreported and cannot support the institutional-type moderator inference as written.

synthesis.rationale: Four independently supported P1 concepts affect the integrity, scope, and evidentiary basis of the central claims; revision is required before the manuscript can be accepted.
